sweep_summary: Zaachila Zapotec is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title produced no first-hand stress statement. The single title-hit, Ariza García's 2016 Aarhus MA thesis (Glottolog 571624), is the one work that should state stress placement (a 'suprasegmental analysis'), but no digital copy exists anywhere reachable: no DOI, no repository record, no archive. it stays a high-priority acquisition (Aarhus University Library or the author). this search of works with stress in the title did turn up and download the author's open 2018 follow-up (Acta Linguistica Petropolitana XIV(2), DOI 10.30842/alp2306573714220, via CyberLeninka), which cites the thesis (pp. 120-126) for Zaachila's four tones and four phonation types but says in footnote 1 that 'The analysis of stress is out of the scope of this study' — so it is silent on word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Ariza-García, Andrea (2018). Phonation types and tones in Zapotec languages: a synchronic comparison. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana XIV(2): 485-516. DOI 10.30842/alp2306573714220.
tone_statements.quote: Zaachila Zapotec and San Lucas Quiaviní Zapotec have the same interaction patterns between the four contrastive phonation types and the four tones. … Table 7. Zaachila Zapotec tone and voice combinations ZAACHILA ZAPOTEC H L F R … in San Lucas Quiaviní Zapotec and Zaachila Zapotec only low and falling tones can co-occur with all the contrastive phonation types. … In both languages rising tone does not co-occur with non-modal vowels. Breathy voice is the only non-modal phonation that does not co-occur with high tone, being restricted to low and falling tones.

sources.citation: Ariza-García, Andrea (2018). Phonation types and tones in Zapotec languages: a synchronic comparison. Acta Linguistica Petropolitana XIV(2): 485-516. DOI 10.30842/alp2306573714220.
sources.quote: Unlike most languages, Zapotec languages display exceptional prosodic patterns consisting of tone, phonation types and stress1. This study focus on how tone and phonation types interact providing a preliminary typological framework. [...] 1 The analysis of stress is out of the scope of this study.
sources.locator: p. 485 (Introduction) and footnote 1; Zaachila data at pp. 496-502 (examples 4a, 6b; Table 7) citing Ariza-García 2016: 120-126
sources.note: Silent on placement. p. 485: 'Zapotec languages display exceptional prosodic patterns consisting of tone, phonation types and stress' with footnote 1 'The analysis of stress is out of the scope of this study.' Zaachila Zapotec data (pp. 496-502, exx. 4a, 6b, Table 7, citing Ariza-García 2016: 120-126) give four tones (H, L, F, R) and four phonation types (modal, breathy, laryngealized, glottalized); disyllabic examples such as [ná.zà] 'I grab', [nà.jàʔ] 'my hand', [lḛ́.jà̰] 'close' are marked for tone only, no stress marks.

tone.locator: §6, pp. 501–502 (section opening on p. 501; Table 7 and the co-occurrence paragraph on p. 502)
tone.says: Four contrastive tones, high, low, falling and rising, on vowels that also carry a four-way phonation contrast; rising only on modal vowels, breathy vowels only low or falling. Stress not treated.

sources.note: No phonology. Locations: San Raymundo Jalpan, south of Oaxaca City past Xoxo, Zaachila, San Bartolo Coyotepec, San Pablo Cuatro Venados, Santa María Coyotepec; 85% intelligibility with Yatzeche, 75% Tilquiapan, 72% San Juan Guelavía; ~550 speakers (1990).

sources.citation: Radin, Paul. 1925. The distribution and phonetics of the Zapotec dialects: a preliminary sketch. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 17: 27-76. (hh.bib hvw:Radin:Zapotec, overview;comparative;wordlist; language code includes Zaachila [ztx])
sources.note: No statement of word-stress placement for Zaachila or any dialect. Zaachila is his dialect area 'II. Zaachila and all the puebloes of Tlacolula and del Centro' (p. 30) with a few Zaachila items illustrating vowel-ending contrasts (p. 31: 'bang! mbal; compadre bal; if not, mbál; mother yuna..'). Only prosodic remark is general to Zapotec: 'The vowels are characterized by the possession of pitch accent' (p. 31) and 'loss of old pitch accent' as a change factor (p. 34). Zaachila wordlist entries carry his acute-type marks but no stress rule is given.

sources.note: The only descriptive phonology of the language and explicitly a suprasegmental analysis; the author's 2018 article cites its tone/phonation chapter (pp. 120-126) and states Zapotec prosody comprises tone, phonation and stress, so this is where a Zaachila stress rule would be stated. Not held by Aarhus/Royal Danish Library catalogues, not in Hammarström's collection, no repository copy: obtain from the author or the Aarhus linguistics department.
